Description: Layer 5. Physical data models for specific applications, derived from Domain and Process models (greenfield) or reverse-engineered from existing databases (brownfield).

A reusable set of attributes that entities follow: Entity, Identifiable, Lifecycleable, Addressable, RoleHolder, Classifiable, Temporal. Each entity declares the attributes itself and lists the base types it follows in edmComposes; the contract for each is in config/edm-rules.yaml (decision D2).
*What* the business can do. A noun-phrase. Modeled in the Domain layer. Distinct from Process (*how* it's executed).
The placement of a business record under a node of a taxonomy. Recorded, with its history, in transaction_hierarchy (decision D11).
Nested under Foundation. Holds reusable construction material: composite value types and the generic taxonomy model.
Layer 3. Capability-aligned stable nouns. Each business function (HR, Finance, Sales, etc.) owns its piece, one model per subdomain.
Enterprise Data Model. This project.
The semantic anchor of the EDM: every Foundation concept is an Entity and carries entity_id.
The globally unique surrogate identifier (UUID) every Entity carries. Stable across all systems, reorganizations, integrations.
A closed list of allowed values, held as an enum on the attribute that uses it (decision D3). Examples: lifecycle states, role types.
Layer 1. Permanent enterprise concepts: Person, Organization (LegalEntity, OrganizationalUnit), Team, Role, Activity, Agreement, Asset, Address, Document, Period.
A business key (e.g., employee_number, tax_id, vendor_number). Lives on canonical entities via Identifiable when enterprise-issued, or in application models when vendor-issued.
A reference that may point to more than one kind of entity, held as a pair <name>_entity_type + <name>_entity_id with no relationship. The allowed types are listed in config/edm-rules.yaml.
A versioned workflow specification. Multiple versions may coexist; instances bind to a single version for life.
A live execution of a Process Definition. Bound immutably to a single definition version (Frozen-Contract principle).
Layer 4. Workflows and instances. References Domain entities; never modifies them (Borrower principle).
The values of a code list or taxonomy (countries, currencies, job families). Data, not schema: the EDM stores the rules for these values, never the values themselves.
A time-bound engagement of a Person or Organization with another party. The universal pivot for "who plays what with whom" relationships. Specialized in Domain (EmployeeRole, Candidate, etc.).
Pattern in Application layer: every application record that mirrors an entity owned elsewhere records its source system and source id.
The Domain-layer entity a ProcessInstance operates on. Captured by subject_entity_id + subject_entity_type.
System-generated identifier (UUID) that never changes. Distinct from natural keys (business identifiers that may change). Both coexist in the EDM.
A hierarchical classification (categories and their containment). Stored as data in the Common taxonomy model, with full version history (decision D11).
The append-only record of which taxonomy node a business record was classified under, when, and with which paths. "Transaction" here means any classified business record, not a financial transaction.

A self-contained composite value structure with no independent identity, reused by external reference. Examples: AmountType (value + currency), QuantityType (value + unit), DocumentType, StateTransition, NaturalIdentifier.
EDM metadata stored on a model object (for example foundationKind, entityType, steward). Configured in hackolade/customProperties/ and checked by tools/.
Creating a model from one or more polyglot models (polyglotDerive). The parent stays the master; the derived model keeps local changes as deviations and is refreshed with polyglotUpdate.
A local change a derived model makes to an entity it inherited. Deviations on entities derived from Foundation or Common are not allowed; others need a deviationReason.
Reuse of an entity, attribute or definition from another model file by relative path. Read-only in the model that uses it; refreshed with extRefUpdate.
A reusable structure inside one model, such as a value type.
A model for one target technology (for example PostgreSQL), from which Hackolade generates DDL.
A technology-neutral logical model. Foundation, Common, Domain and Process models are polyglot models.
Hackolade's inheritance construct: a supertype, its subtypes, and the strategy that decides how inheritance becomes tables.
Coarse entity-level state (Active, Inactive, Archived, etc.). Lives on entities via the Lifecycleable base type. Distinct from process workflow state.
A recorded change from one lifecycle state to another. Stored in state_history on Lifecycleable entities.
Fine-grained state managed by ProcessInstance. Distinct from entity-level lifecycle state.
A capability's "turf" — the set of entities it owns and is the primary steward for. One polyglot model per bounded context.
Process references Domain; Process never modifies Domain.
Domain models capabilities (what the business is) rather than processes (how it runs).
A ProcessInstance's binding to a definition version is set at instance creation and never changes.
There can be only one. Each concept exists once across the enterprise.
Dependencies flow upward only. Foundation knows nothing of Application.
An enforceable constraint backed by tooling and tests. Distinct from a principle (aspirational).
Each Domain entity has exactly one primary-steward capability that owns it.
Before placing anything in Common, ask: "Would another enterprise with a different business need this?"
Roles do not mutate core terms. Changes end one Role and begin another, preserving history.
See Primary Stewardship.
Every ProcessDefinition is versioned; instances bind to a snapshot.
